    if t.dim() == 0:

    elif t.dim() == 1:

    return -x[..., 0] * y[..., 0] + (x[..., 1:] * y[..., 1:]).sum(dim=-1)

    n = torch.sqrt(n2).clamp_min(1e-15)

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: m_pi := o for all levels, i.e. w_k = PT_{o->a}(theta_hat_{l,k}) and the anchor table is never consulted - a curvature-only transport RQ with zero behaviour input.
ideas.ablation_both_on: table-built anchors plus two-leg transport, i.e. the trained candidate.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: PT := identity and exp/log := identity (plain additive residual recursion), so w_k = theta_{l,k} and r_{l} = r_{l-1} - theta_{l,k_l}: exactly the baseline Euclidean RQ, in which m has no effect on any computed value.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage 2 training split only: a sparse row-normalised transition matrix T (row i = next-item counts after i, symmetric-free, no self loops). Every 25 epochs, a no-grad encoder pass over all training items yields current prefixes pi(i) and normalised codes z~_i; for each prefix pi at level l-1, t_pi(j) = sum_{i in S_pi} T_ij / sum_{i in S_pi} sum_{j'} T_ij', and v_pi = clip(sum_j t_pi(j) z~_j). Table entries are frozen between refreshes and detached from autograd.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transition mass from training sequences, aggregated over the cohort of items that currently share a prefix.
ideas.cost_estimate: +6 to 10 percent wall clock over baseline Stage 2; no new parameters (same L x K x D codebook tensor), table is at most (L-1)*K*D floats, per step the transports are two rank-1 updates on a K x D block per item (about 100 MFLOP extra per step at batch 1023, L=3, K=256, D=32), and the anchor refresh is 120 no-grad full-passes over 24556 items (about 1.3 percent of the 3000-epoch budget). Stage 3 unchanged.

ideas.coupling_path: prefix tokens -> anchor-table lookup m -> two-leg transport -> the code frame w_k and residual frame r used by the argmin -> token k_l -> next prefix -> Stage 3 SID. Removing the behaviour removes m (m = o, direct path); removing the curvature makes both transports the identity, so w_k = theta_k and r is plain-subtracted; either removal changes the argmin and hence the tokens.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Keeping the idea requires that the transports change the realized partition and that the change helps: level 2..3 token flip rate against the behaviour-off forward pass is well above zero and concentrated on items with small top-2 hyperbolic distance gaps, prefix-conditional successor entropy falls relative to behaviour-off, and Stage 3 test recall@10 exceeds 0.065 (above the 0.0525-0.0540 behaviour band and the 0.0638 history best).
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ residual recursion itself, at every level l >= 2, in the frame in which the nearest-code assignment and the residual are computed (not a loss term, not a post-hoc re-ranking of codes).
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Unit-hyperboloid (Lorentz) model, fixed negative curvature K = -1 in z~ units (c = 1/s^2 in raw encoder units, s measured, not tuned): parallel transport PT_{u->w}(v) = v + <w,v>_L/(1-<u,w>_L) (u+w), composed as PT_{m->a} o PT_{o->m}; the holonomy of the triangle (o,m,a) equals its area.
ideas.key_change: The code vectors and the residual used at each RQ level are expressed in a frame reached by transporting through the prefix's training-only successor anchor, so the residual direction seen by the quantizer is rotated by the holonomy of (o, m, a); the token at levels 2..L is chosen in that transported frame.
ideas.leakage_boundary: T is built only from training-split sequences and z~ only from training-split items encoded by the Stage 2 encoder; validation and test interactions are never read during Stage 2, the table is rebuilt only inside Stage 2, and Stage 3 consumes the frozen SIDs as before. SID construction for any item depends on statistics of the training cohort, never on that item's own held-out continuation.
ideas.motivation: RQ-VAE Semantic IDs are built by a purely reconstructive residual walk, so deeper tokens split items by residual geometry, not by what users actually do next; behaviour-only prefix cues help (+0.012~0.014) but every curvature term tried so far was add-on and measured inert.
ideas.novelty: Unlike successor-frame warp, branch-geodesic rank, fork-angle transport, cohesion prefix ranking, co-occurrence Frechet, tangent quantization, region argmax, interest-cohort parents, Poincare-Frechet/VQ codebooks, EQVOTE-HYP, HORO, statecell margin, anisotropic Poincare, CURVCTRL, LORENTZ profile smoothing, behcone, succboost-geoshift and BRad-RQ, no codebook statistic, rank, mean, vote or per-level curvature is touched. The curved operation is a parallel-transport composition that carries code tangents o->m->a instead of o->a, where m is the behaviour successor anchor of the already-decided prefix. Because hyperbolic transport is path dependent (holonomy = triangle area) and Euclidean transport is the identity, the mechanism's entire effect is exactly the curvature; curvature-off reproduces baseline RQ bit for bit, so the geometry switch cannot be inert.
ideas.observables: level-1 tokens identical to behaviour-off by construction; level 2..3 token flip rate against the behaviour-off forward pass at the same checkpoint; hyperbolic top-2 distance gap of flipped items (should be small); prefix-conditional successor entropy; code-norm invariance check ||w_k||_{g(a)} = ||theta_k||_{g(o)}; Stage 3 test_recall@10.

holonomy angles are O(1) rad and may over-rotate level 2..3 partitions and hurt reconstruction; the encoder/anchor table co-evolution may collapse all anchors toward the same point, making the path degenerate and the coupling

inert; the successor anchor may be dominated by globally popular items, adding no prefix-specific direction; extra autograd through exp/log/transport could slow or destabilise training; single-run seed noise is comparable to the expected gain.
ideas.safeguards: clamp arcosh arguments to >= 1+1e-6; compute the Lorentz inner products and the denominators 1-<u,w>_L (>= 2 always) in float64; re-project a to <a,a>_L = -1 after every exp and every transport; project tangents to T_a; clip ||theta_{l,k}|| to Q99(||Z~||)/L (measured once, frozen) and clip the anchor tangent norm to Q99(||Z~||); prefixes with < 5 items or zero outgoing mass use m = o; deterministic lowest-index tie-break in the argmin; anchor table built no-grad and stored detached, refreshed only between epochs; log (never gate on) the median anchor norm and the flip rate so a degenerate path is visible.
ideas.spec_equations: SPECIFICATION CORRECTION (second). The first run took the same codeword for every item: in the Lorentz model the difference of the residual and a codeword is not spacelike, so neither <r - W, r - W>_L nor its negation is a distance, and the arg-min of either degenerated. The assignment and the objective therefore use the COSINE form on the HYPERBOLOID IMAGE of the residual: with rhat_b = exp_o(r_b) (r_b is the spatial residual, lifted for the update), d2[b,k] = -<rhat_b, W[b,k]>_L = rhat_b0*W0 - sum_{i>0} rhat_bi*Wi, which is cosh of the hyperbolic distance between the two hyperboloid points: its arg-min is the nearest transported codeword and its value is at least 1, so the term added to the objective is positive. (The residual alone is NOT a point of the hyperboloid: its Minkowski product with a codeword collapses to a Euclidean dot product whose arg-min is the farthest codeword, which is what collapsed the first two attempts.) Everything else is unchanged: parameters theta_{l,k} in R^D, lift theta_hat = (0, theta), s = RMS(Z_0) frozen, Minkowski <x,y>_L = -x_0 y_0 + x_{1:}.y_{1:}, o = (1,0..0), log_o(u) = arcosh(u_0) u_{1:}/|u_{1:}|, exp_o(v) = (cosh|v|, sinh|v| v/|v|), exp_u(v) = cosh|v|_L u + sinh|v|_L v/|v|_L, log_u(w) = d (w + <u,w>_L u)/|w + <u,w>_L u|, d = arcosh(-<u,w>_L), PT_{u->w}(v) = v + <w,v>_L/(1-<u,w>_L) (u+w). Forward: r = Z/s lifted (0,r), a = o. For l=1..L: v_pi = M[prefix] (0 if l=1, use_behaviour off, or missing); m = exp_o(v_pi); W[b,k] = exp_{a_b}(PT_{m_b->a_b}(PT_{o->m_b}(theta_{l,k}))); (a parallel transport moves a TANGENT vector, so the codeword is carried as the tangent vector theta_{l,k} and read back as a point; without the exponential the transported codeword leaves the hyperboloid and the assignment degenerates.) d2[b,k] = -<r_b, W[b,k]>_L; k_l = argmin_k d2[b,k] (lowest index wins); e = r_b - W[b,k_l] transported from the old frame a_b to the new frame; a_b <- the chosen transported codeword; r_b <- PT_{a_old -> a_new}(e).

ideas.ablation_geometry_off: c->0 flat analogue: exp_0 replaced by v -> v/lambda, d_P by Euclidean, budget kept as (1-q)(||.||+||.||)/lambda.

q_ij -> budget m_ij -> hinge h_ij(k) -> score J_i(k) -> argmin -> SID. Removing behaviour zeroes the hinge (score becomes a monotone reparametrisation of Euclidean nearest-residual); removing curvature rep

ideas.hyperbolic_location: inside the RQ residual quantizer, in the per-level code-selection argmin and in the training loss term of the chosen code.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: exp_0/log at the origin of the Poincare ball of fixed negative curvature c=1, Poincare distance d_P, and the induced Gromov-product/geodesic separation scale; no trainable curvature.
ideas.key_change: Each level's code is chosen by argmin of one score = hyperbolic squared distance from the candidate partial-code point to the curved target point, PLUS a behaviour-weighted one-sided hinge on the hyperbolic distance between the item's candidate partial-code point and its training successor's partial-code point (two-sweep per batch: sweep 1 freezes reference codes, sweep 2 re-assigns).
ideas.leakage_boundary: T built once from the Stage-2 training sequences only; no validation/test interaction, session or item statistic enters; matrix frozen and hashed before epoch 0.
ideas.motivation: Baseline RQ-VAE decides every SID level by Euclidean nearest-residual, so the prefix hierarchy the Stage-3 generator must learn is whatever the latent geometry happens to make close; how users actually move (which item deterministically follows which) is never expressed as prefix structure. ideas.novelty: Not a per-item or per-level radial target (BRad-RQ, CURVCTRL), not a Fréchet codebook, not transport/tangent/cone/rank. The new object is a FRACTIONAL GEODESIC BUDGET m_ij^l = (1-q_ij)*(rho_i+rho_j): the relative mass q_ij of a training transition licenses a hyperbolic separation of at most that fraction of the maximal separation in curvature -1, and this budget enters the argmin that PRODUCES the SID, not a side loss.
ideas.observables: shared-prefix count of top-mass transition pairs, rank correlation between q_ij and shared-prefix count, per-level code-usage entropy, per-level radius distribution, collision/validity counts, Stage-3 test_R@10.
risks: SID collapse under pull; sparse tail transitions; boundary gradient blow-up; sweep-1/sweep-2 inconsistency; curvature again adding nothing measurable.

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.

papers.abstract: In the last few decades, the kernel method has been successfully used in the field of adaptive filtering to solve nonlinear problems. Mercer kernel is used to map data from input space to reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) by kernel adaptive filter (KAF). In regenerated kernel Hilbert spaces, the inner product can be easily calculated by computing the so-called kernel trick. The Kernel adaptive filtering algorithm is superior to common adaptive filtering algorithm in solving nonlinear problems and nonlinear channel equalization. papers.abstract: We present a novel vector quantization (VQ) module for the two state-of-the-art long-range simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) algorithms. The VQ task in SLAM is generally performed using unsupervised methods. We provide an alternative approach trough embedding a semisupervised hyperbolic graph convolutional neural network (HGCN) in the VQ step of the SLAM processes. The SLAM platforms we have utilized for this purpose are fast appearance-based mapping (FABMAP) and oriented fast and rotated short (ORB), both of which rely on extracting the features of the captured images in their loop closure detection (LCD) module. For the first time, we have considered the space formed by these SURF features, robust image descriptors, as a graph, enabling us to apply an HGCN in the VQ section which results in an improved LCD performance. papers.abstract: Residual Vector Quantization turns continuous representations into discrete, multi-level token sequences. Yet most methods operate in Euclidean space, despite the coarse-to-fine structure of the resulting codes and the latent hierarchies present in many data domains. Hyperbolic geometry offers a natural alternative for hierarchical representations, but naive hyperbolic extensions introduce geometric inconsistencies: non-associative hyperbolic addition prevents consistent residual aggregation, while standard straight-through gradient estimation ignores the geometry of the latent space. We propose a geometry-aware hyperbolic residual quantization that addresses these issues in both the forward and backward passes. In the forward pass, Hyperbolic Residual Aggregation restores the telescoping behavior of residual quantization on the Poincare ball. In the backward pass, a discounted Hyperbolic Straight-Through Estimator routes the reconstruction gradient through the quantizer as a single geometric block, avoiding unstable recursive gradient transport across residual stages. papers.abstract: Most high-performance block-coding systems for image compression, such as JPEG, have been designed for software or dedicated digital hardware implementations where the data are already assumed to be available in digital format. In modern CMOS photosensors, smart-pixel technologies have allowed the realization of basic signal processing tasks at the pixel level, in analog format before analog-to-digital (A/D) conversion. The elimination of A/D converters and implementation of block-coding directly over analog blocks of pixels in such sensors can be attractive both in terms of area savings and power consumption. The design of block encoders, under the strong hardware constraints that derive from the A/D converter removal, has been investigated in this paper. We present a comparison of three systems in terms of rate, distortion and complexity, and present a numerical simulation analysis of their sensitivity to implementation errors. papers.title: Sensitivity analysis of low-complexity vector quantizers for focal-plane image compression

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
papers.title: Representation Collapsing Problems in Vector Quantization

papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been shown to be highly effective in solving optimization problems in a wide range of applications. Such algorithms typically use gradient descent with backpropagation and the chain rule. Hence, the backpropagation fails if intermediate gradients are zero for some functions in the computational graph, because it causes the gradients to collapse when multiplying with zero. Vector quantization is one of those challenging functions for machine learning algorithms, since it is a piece-wise constant function and its gradient is zero almost everywhere. A typical solution is to apply the straight through estimator which simply copies the gradients over the vector quantization function in the backpropagation. Other solutions are based on smooth or stochastic approximation. This study proposes a vector quantization technique called NSVQ, which approximates the vector quantization behavior by substituting a multiplicative noise so that it can be used for machine learning problems. papers.title: NSVQ: Noise Substitution in Vector Quantization for Machine Learning

papers.abstract: We establish stable quantum ergodicity for spin Hamiltonians, also known as Pauli-Schrödinger operators. Our approach combines new analytic techniques of mixed quantization, inspired by local index theory, with stable ergodicity results for partially hyperbolic systems.
